english: In a hall the rows of seats are numbered $1,2,3,\dots$. The first row has $4$ seats, every row has more seats than the row before it, and the increases in the number of seats from one row to the next form an arithmetic progression. The third row has $18$ seats and the sixth row has $69$ seats. Then the total number of seats in the first $10$ rows is
hindi: एक सभागार में सीटों की पंक्तियाँ $1,2,3,\dots$ क्रमांकित हैं। पहली पंक्ति में $4$ सीटें हैं, प्रत्येक पंक्ति में उससे पहले वाली पंक्ति से अधिक सीटें हैं, तथा एक पंक्ति से अगली पंक्ति में सीटों की संख्या में होने वाली वृद्धियाँ एक समान्तर श्रेढ़ी बनाती हैं। तीसरी पंक्ति में $18$ सीटें तथा छठी पंक्ति में $69$ सीटें हैं। तब प्रथम $10$ पंक्तियों में सीटों की कुल संख्या है
solution: Let $u_n$ seats be in row $n$ and $u_{n+1}-u_n=p+(n-1)q$ (an AP). Then $u_n=4+(n-1)p+\dfrac{(n-1)(n-2)}{2}q$
solution_full: Let $u_n$ be the number of seats in row $n$ and let the increases be $u_2-u_1=p$, $u_3-u_2=p+q$, and in general $u_{n+1}-u_n=p+(n-1)q$, an arithmetic progression with first term $p$ and common difference $q$.
From $q=14-2p$: $p+28-4p=13\Rightarrow p=5$, and then $q=4$. The increases $5,9,13,\dots$ are positive, as required.
Hence $u_n=4+5(n-1)+2(n-1)(n-2)=2n^2-n+3$; the first six rows have $4,9,18,31,48,69$ seats, which matches the data.
originality_note: New: the second-order sequence is fixed by two non-consecutive values (rows 3 and 6) instead of a listed run of terms, so the first difference and the common difference of the increases must be solved for (way 5: method of differences linked with a two-equation system). Closest known: 'sum of 3 + 7 + 13 + 21 + ... to n terms' exercises. Different because: no consecutive terms are given, so the general term cannot be read off; it must be built from the AP of differences.
blueprint_concepts: Sum of a sequence for which difference of consecutive terms form an AP
